title: Arjunolic acid ameliorates lipopolysaccharide-induced depressive behavior by inhibiting neuroinflammation via microglial SIRT1/AMPK/Notch1 signaling pathway.
authors: Yang, Ying; Lai, Ying; Tong, Xueli; Li, Zipei; Cheng, Yuanyuan; Tian, Li-Wen
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Arjunolic acid通过SIRT1/AMPK/Notch1通路抑制神经炎症改善抑郁行为，仅涉及小分子-蛋白互作，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Neuroinflammation is involved in the pathogenesis of depression disorder by activating microglia cells, increasing proinflammatory cytokines, effecting serotonin synthesis and metabolism, and neuronal apoptosis and neurogenesis. Arjunolic acid (ARG) is a triterpenoid derived from the fruits of Akebia trifoliata for treating psychiatric disorders in TCM clinic, which exhibits anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. However, its anti-depressive effect and underlying mechanism are unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: The aim of this study is to explore the effect of arjunolic acid on depression and its possible mechanisms. METHODS: Intraperitoneal injection of LPS in mice and LPS stimulated-BV2 microglia were utilized to set up in vivo and in vitro models. Behavioral tests, H&E staining and ELISA were employed to evaluate the effect of arjunolic acid on depression. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, molecular docking and Western blot were performed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Arjunolic acid dramatically ameliorated depressive behavior in LPS-induced mice. The levels of BDNF and 5-HT in the hippocampus of the mice were increased, while the number of iNOS + IBA1+ cells in the brain were decreased and Arg1+IBA1+ positive cells were increased after arjunolic acid treatment. In addition, arjunolic acid promoted the polarization of BV2 microglia from M1 to M2 type. Notably, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking technologies identified SIRT1 as the target of arjunolic acid. Moreover, after SIRT1 inhibition by using EX-527, the effects of arjunolic acid on ameliorating LPS-induced depressive behavior in mice and promoting M2 Microglia polarization were blocked. In addition, arjunolic acid activated AMPK and decreased Notch1 expression, however, inhibition of AMPK, the effect of arjunolic acid on the downregulation of Notch1 expression were weaken. CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates that arjunolic acid suppressed neuroinflammation through modulating the SIRT1/AMPK/Notch1 signaling pathway. Our study demonstrates that arjunolic acid might serve as a potiential anti-depressant.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：神经炎症通过激活小胶质细胞、增加促炎细胞因子、影响血清素合成与代谢以及神经元凋亡和神经发生，参与抑郁症的发病机制。阿江榄仁酸（Arjunolic acid, ARG）是一种从三叶木通（Akebia trifoliata）果实中提取的三萜类化合物，在中医临床上用于治疗精神疾病，具有抗炎和神经保护作用。然而，其抗抑郁效果及潜在机制尚不清楚。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨阿江榄仁酸对抑郁症的作用及其可能机制。方法：通过小鼠腹腔注射脂多糖（LPS）和LPS刺激的BV2小胶质细胞建立体内和体外模型。采用行为学测试、H&E染色和ELISA评估阿江榄仁酸对抑郁症的作用。通过RT-qPCR、免疫荧光、分子对接和Western blot阐明分子机制。结果：阿江榄仁酸显著改善了LPS诱导小鼠的抑郁样行为。治疗后，小鼠海马中BDNF和5-HT水平升高，而脑内iNOS+IBA1+细胞数量减少，Arg1+IBA1+阳性细胞增加。此外，阿江榄仁酸促进BV2小胶质细胞从M1型向M2型极化。值得注意的是，药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）和分子对接技术鉴定出SIRT1为阿江榄仁酸的靶点。此外，使用EX-527抑制SIRT1后，阿江榄仁酸改善LPS诱导小鼠抑郁样行为及促进M2小胶质细胞极化的作用被阻断。另外，阿江榄仁酸激活AMPK并降低Notch1表达，但抑制AMPK后，阿江榄仁酸下调Notch1表达的作用减弱。结论：本研究阐明阿江榄仁酸通过调节SIRT1/AMPK/Notch1信号通路抑制神经炎症。我们的研究表明，阿江榄仁酸可能作为一种潜在的抗抑郁药物。
